title: Method for measuring solubilities of slightly soluble gases in liquids
experimental_method: Gas burette volumetric method: gas saturated with water vapour is dissolved in outgassed water at constant pressure of 1 atm in a stirred thermostatted vessel and the volume of gas dissolved is read directly on the mercury-levelled burette.
uncertainties_stated: Apparatus precision 0.2 %; thermostat +-0.03 C; estimated error from diffusion through capillaries at most 0.01 %; neglect of solvent expansion on dissolution (partial molar volume correction about half of the estimated total error) not applied.
quality_remarks: Authors' argon values are systematically higher than Lannung and Morrison and Johnstone, which they attribute to incomplete saturation in the earlier work. Supersaturation (about 1 % high) observed with too vigorous stirring; procedure avoids it. Temperature scale not stated. Argon is outside the seven gases of the brief but is kept per SPEC v2.1 convention 1.
